params must match the schema; a valid example is included

space.description: 'model' (design space, US survey feet) or a sheet id/name (paper space, inches), e.g. 'SH-001' or 'C-101'

layer.description: layer name; defaults to the current layer

target.description: an explicit point for the leader to point at, in the callout's own space (paper inches on a sheet); prefer target_entity or target_anchor, which cannot miss

target_entity.description: what to point at, by id (find_entities and hit_test return them; reference elements are 'DESIGN:LN-004'). The engine computes a point on it, so a curve is aimed at correctly. On a sheet it may be a model or referenced entity: the tip lands where the viewport shows it. Give exactly one of target / target_entity / target_anchor.

at.description: where along target_entity the leader TIP goes: start|mid|end or a fraction 0-1 (default mid) -- not where the text goes, which is position. From a sheet it runs along the part of the entity that sheet shows, so mid is always a point the reader can see

target_anchor.description: a station, offset or named point of an alignment to point at: '586+57.73@20.83L', 'PC-1', {station, offset}. There is no entity at a station, so this is how a station-and-offset callout is aimed

alignment.description: the alignment target_anchor is on; a referenced one is 'DESIGN:SR-100' (read, not owned -- the callout carries no anchor). Defaults to the document's only alignment

viewport.description: on a sheet, the viewport to see the target through (default: the first one that shows it)

position.description: where the text sits, clear of the geometry, in the callout's own space. The text reads away from the target: when the target is to the left, the text starts here and runs right (left-justified); when it is to the right, the text ends here (right-justified). Vertically it is centred on this point, and the landing runs from here back toward the target

content.description: the callout's text; \n starts a new line

height.description: text height in space units (feet in model, inches on sheets); defaults to the annotation scale in model space, 0.10 in on a sheet

landing.description: horizontal shoulder at the text (default 2.5 x height; 0 for none)
